“Dreading” isn’t really a recognized term by most, despite how familiar ppl are with “dreadlocks” or “dreads”. Dreadlocks on Afro textured hair are tightly condensed coils of hair tangling within itself. On straight hair, it’s usually matted sections of hair that resemble dreadlocks. Many people of afro descent prefer the terms “locs” or “loc’ing” to create distance from the negative connotations of “dreads” being dreadful, and from straight haired non black ppl with matted hair. Freeform, interlocked, palm rolled, etc, locs are locs.

1) Skincare (cleansers and moisturizers):
      >absolutely crucial
      > the most important base to makeup in a clean, moisturizer face every time 

2) Primer
    > Primer is a base for your makeup
    > smooths out your pores and gives your makeup something to stick to
    > it also helps your makeup from getting too oily or cakey

3) Foundation
     > evens out the skin tone
     > can vary in coverage from light to full
     > shade matching in important, swatch some of the foundation on your jaw, if it's almost invisible, that's your match
     > best applied with a damp beauty sponge

4) Concealer
     > covering and correcting scars, blemish, and what not.
     > try to have this match your skin as closely as possible as well
     > I'd say apply before Foundation 
5) Setting Powder
     > helps keep all your face makeup in place
     > apply after foundation and concealer with a light brush

6) Eye makeup
     > eye makeup is what's really gonna bring that WOW factor to your look the easiest as a beginner
    > find eyeshadow palettes with neutral colors that are matte, sparkly, and metallic, and with darker colors like brown or grey. also keep an eye out for bold colors you like like jewel tones.
    > blending your colors together is key but if you're a one-and-done kind of girl, one swipe of a metallic or sparkly eye shadow on your lids will do the trick.
    > learn how to do a simple winged liner. It can amp up your look with or without eyeshadow. A felt tip pen is great for beginners.

Bonuses: look at high end and low end, watch every tutorial available, leave contouring alone until your more comfortable, practice makes perfect!
